The Facility Coding Supervisor provides administrative leadership and technical oversight for inpatient and outpatient facility coding operations. This position is responsible for supervising coding personnel, coordinating workforce resources, monitoring coding performance and quality metrics, and optimizing the use of Computer-Assisted Coding (CAC) technology across the network. The supervisor serves as a subject matter expert in hospital facility coding while partnering with leadership to improve coding quality, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and coding technology performance. The Facility Coding Supervisor analyzes coding production, quality, precision and recall reporting, audit findings, and workforce metrics to identify trends, recommend process improvements, and enhance the effectiveness and reliability of coding workflows. This position also provides administrative oversight of personnel activities while ensuring compliance with organizational policies, collective bargaining requirements where applicable.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and other standard reporting applications.
Strong understanding of Computer-Assisted Coding (CAC) functionality, coding quality principles, productivity measurement, and coding workflow processes.
Knowledge of University and Medical Center organizations, policies, procedures and forms
Must demonstrate customer service skills appropriate to the job
Expert knowledge of ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, HCPCS Level II, Official Coding Guidelines, Medicare reimbursement methodologies, and hospital facility coding compliance
Exercises sound judgment and accountability in making timely operational and administrative decisions while recognizing when leadership consultation is appropriate.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English

Excellent leadership, organizational, communication, conflict resolution, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills with the ability to supervise coding staff, manage multiple priorities, and foster a collaborative work environment.
Demonstrated analytical skills with the ability to identify trends and develop actionable recommendations
Ability to maintain a work pace appropriate to the workload
Ability to independently research issues, evaluate available resources, and develop appropriate solutions
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships across the Health System, School of Medicine, UCI Research Administration and other UC System campuses

Ability to communicate professionally, respectfully, diplomatically, and tactfully with employees, physicians, leadership, and interdisciplinary teams, including providing constructive feedback and navigating difficult conversations.
